summary: The note surveys how street art and graffiti have moved from being seen as vandalism to recognized art forms, focusing on emerging artists in Jaisalmer and in Mexico City, Lisbon, New York and Berlin. It describes specific artists and projects, international influences, tech-driven interactive murals, and festivals. It closes by raising the challenge of preserving street art's ephemeral quality, citing the Jaisalmer Street Art Preservation Society.
one_line: Overview of emerging street artists and graffiti movements in Jaisalmer, Mexico City, Lisbon, New York and Berlin, plus preservation challenges.
key_facts: Street art and graffiti have surpassed the vandalism label to become recognized as transformative and legitimate art forms.
Arav Nair's first landmark mural, "Desert Bloom", appeared in Jaisalmer in 2023 and mixes folklore stories with a modern twist.
Reena Kumari has been a symbol of empowerment for women since November 2023, with works featuring strong, defiant women on old walls of local markets.
On January 20, 2024, Brazilian artist Paulo Terra collaborated with Jaisalmer artists, drawing international attention to climate change and the peace movement.
Ankit Patel's "Augmented Realities", launched February 1, 2020, uses QR codes in murals to unlock multi-media experiences with soundscapes and animated scenes.
The first Jaisalmer Street Art Festival took place in 2024, where Dia Kapoor's use of Phad paint techniques on urban structures received critical acclaim.
Sol Robles' "Urban Heartbeat" series in Mexico City began in September 2023 and celebrates Mexicano identity across neighborhoods and classes.
Joao Silva's "Lisbon Layers", revealed in December 2023, combines traditional azulejo tiles with graffiti and features historical themes and calls for social change.
Nadia Gonzalez's "Streets Symphony" in New York was introduced on October 2, 2023 (written "20,23" in the note) and used spray-paint and discarded items in overlooked Brooklyn corners.
Karl Schmidt's "Walls of Change" murals in Berlin began in early September 2023 and criticize political stagnation while inspiring Berlin's youth.
The Jaisalmer Street Art Preservation Society was established on August 3rd, 2024 to preserve and maintain street art for future generations.
Jaisalmer's emerging artists reflect a global conversation that includes Banksy and Eduardo Kobra.
The note names both Arav Kumari and Arav Nair, and Reena Nair and Reena Kumari, so the artists' names are inconsistent.
